captions.caption: A man in a plaid shirt kneels in a chicken brooder with many small chicks.
A man introduces himself and the topic of increasing space for baby chicks.
The man in the flannel shirt gestures towards chicks huddled under red heat lamps.
A man explains why he is expanding the brooder area for his yellow chicks.
While kneeling in the brooder, the man discusses specific spacing for chicks.
The man looks directly at the camera while talking in the chicken brooder.
A man gestures to the area where many yellow chicks are currently gathered.
The man explains management practices for young chicks in a wooden brooder.
In the brooder, the man talks about how chicks' space needs change as they grow.
The man finishes his introductory remarks as a logo starts to appear.
The Farm Marketing Solutions logo is shown on a gray background.
The words "Farm Marketing Solutions" are displayed with a farm icon.
The logo animation continues to play on the screen.
The logo is fully visible with the farm and silo graphic.
The logo remains on the screen before the scene changes.
The video shows a man talking in a chicken brooder with several heat lamps.
A man continues discussing the management of Cornish Cross chicks.
The man explains that Cornish Cross chicks are raised as broilers for meat.
A man gestures towards the large group of yellow chicks in the brooder.
The man explains that small chicks can get confused if their area is too large.
In the brooder, the man points to heat lamps and the huddled chicks.
The man describes the risk of chicks wandering too far from food or water.
A man explains the importance of tight spacing for very young chicks.
The man uses his hands to demonstrate a concentrated area in the brooder.
While kneeling, the man looks at the camera and continues his explanation.
The man talks about the benefits of keeping young chicks closer together.
A man gestures towards red heat lamps providing warmth to the chicks.
The man mentions how his setup helps chicks find food and water easily.
In the brooder, the man looks around while explaining chick management.
A man notes that chicks require more space as they grow larger.
The man explains that Cornish Cross chicks grow at a very fast rate.
A man gestures to yellow chicks moving on the wood shavings floor.
While kneeling among equipment, the man continues his explanation.
The man looks at the camera and talks about expanding the chick brooder.
A man prepares to demonstrate the process of adding space to the brooder.
The man picks up a large, heavy bale of wood shavings in the brooder.
Using a utility knife, the man cuts through the plastic wrap on the bale.
The man continues cutting the bale's packaging while kneeling on the floor.
A man pulls the plastic wrap away from a compressed block of wood shavings.
The man starts spreading fresh wood shavings onto the brooder floor.
A man tips a large bale of shavings over to release the bedding material.
The man pulls paper packaging off a large block of compressed shavings.
A man continues to remove paper wrapping from the compressed bedding.
In the expansion area, the man works to unpack the wood shavings.
The man pulls more of the paper packaging away from the wood shavings.
A man starts breaking up the large block of compressed wood shavings.
The man tosses the empty paper packaging out of the new brooder area.
A man begins to spread the wood shavings across the brooder floor.
The man uses his hands to distribute fresh bedding in the expansion space.
A man continues spreading wood shavings to cover the bare floor.
Working on a pile of shavings, the man spreads them toward the wall.
The man continues to distribute wood shavings across the floor with his hands.
A man spreads more shavings from the central pile to the floor.
The man ensures the floor is evenly covered with fresh wood shavings.
A man continues working on the large amount of wood shavings on the floor.
The man pulls shavings from a pile and pushes them across the brooder floor.
Near a wooden partition, the man prepares the expansion area with shavings.
A man continues the process of spreading bedding material in the brooder.
The man uses broad arm motions to scatter shavings over the wood floor.
A man finishes spreading the wood shavings from the first bale.
